findings.issue: Unsanitized `sort` query parameter is interpolated directly into a SQL ORDER BY clause, enabling SQL injection
findings.evidence: `const sort = (req.query.sort as string) || 'r.created_at DESC';` passed to `Stats.getReviewsSorted(bookId, sort)`, which builds `ORDER BY ${sort}` in stats.ts:46 — only the `?` placeholder for bookId is parameterized, the ORDER BY text is raw. No whitelist, unlike the sibling `getBooksPage` which validates against `BOOK_SORT_COLUMNS`.

findings.issue: Rating validation condition uses `&&` instead of `||`, making the bounds check always false and effectively a no-op
findings.evidence: `if (!Number.isInteger(rating) || (rating < 1 && rating > 5))` — no number is both <1 and >5, so any integer (0, -100, 9999) passes and is persisted via `Review.updateReview`. Contrast with the correct `rating < 1 || rating > 5` already used elsewhere in the same file (line ~173).

findings.issue: Unescaped user-controlled `display_name` interpolated into an HTML response, allowing stored XSS
findings.evidence:
`res.send(`
${top.display_name} rated it ${top.rating}/5
`)` — `display_name` is user-settable with no sanitization on write and no escaping on render.

findings.issue: `bookId` from `req.params.id` isn't validated as a number before use in `/books/:id/reviews`, unlike sibling routes
findings.evidence: No NaN check and no `Book.getBookById` existence check; a non-numeric id (e.g. `/books/abc/reviews`) silently returns an empty 200 array instead of 404/400, unlike `/books/:id` and `/books/:id/histogram`.
